games.summary: Thursday's opener is a protection story. Houston gets home after the pass rush to the tune of a sack on more than 9% of dropbacks, and Indianapolis will start backups at both tackle spots on a short week. That's a bad mix for Daniel Jones, who has been the least efficient passer in football over the last three weeks and just watched the front office trade away Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Stroud has been rolling, and Nico Collins is the best player in either receiver room. The one thing that keeps this from being a walkover on paper is the number: the market has run Houston from about 10 to 12.5, while ESPN's FPI makes it closer to a touchdown. The mismatch is real; whether it's two touchdowns' worth is a different question.

details.scheme: Houston's pass rush (9.2% sack rate, second-best) meets an Indianapolis line that allows 7.1% and is without both starting tackles (Raimann, Travis OUT). Stroud is +0.218/db over the same stretch; Nico Collins (+0.436/tgt) is the best receiver on the field.

games.summary: Minnesota wins outright, the boldest call on the board. San Francisco has the best passing offense in the league (+0.298), and Mike Evans is expected back from his Achilles, but he hasn't played in a month and is likely on a pitch count against an elite Vikings pass rush. That rush is the same one that sank Green Bay last week. Cousins has Hockenson and Jennings cleared, the game is in Mexico City, so the Niners don't get a home crowd, and the line drifting to 3.5 adds a hook for the cover. The worry is still Minnesota's offense with Addison out.
